answers.text: Osmosis is the movement of water across a partially permeable membrane from high to low concentration. Diffusion is the net movement of particles down a concentration gradient.

(a) The substrate binds to the active site and the enzyme changes shape to fit it closely, which speeds up the reaction. (b) High temperatures break the bonds in the enzyme so the active site denatures and the substrate cannot fit, lowering the rate.
Losing the nucleus makes room for more haemoglobin so more oxygen is carried.
